1.label: ТЕКСТ
1.title: Orientation Memo
1.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
1.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
1.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
1.text:
Welcome to the Serious Crimes Unit. You will find that the work here rarely resembles what you have seen on television. Most of our time is spent reviewing evidence, interviewing reluctant witnesses and writing reports that nobody wants to read.

You will also notice a man lying on the couch with a cup of tea. His name is Patrick Jane, and he is not, strictly speaking, a member of staff. He is a consultant who used to make a living as a television psychic. He claims that he possesses no supernatural abilities whatsoever; he simply observes what other people overlook.

Agent Lisbon tolerates his methods because, frustratingly, they tend to work. You are advised not to bet against him, not to lend him money and, above all, not to let him read your face during your first week.

items.q: What is Patrick Jane's official role?
How does Jane explain his abilities?
Why does Lisbon tolerate his methods?
Which sentence uses a stative verb correctly?
options: He is possessing no special abilities.

items.q: Which sentence describes a temporary situation?
options: Jane is staying in the office this week.
Jane stays in the office this week since years.

2.label: ТЕКСТ
2.title: The Grey Envelope
2.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
2.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
2.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
2.text:
Five years ago Patrick Jane was the most famous psychic in California. He had been appearing on daytime television for months, and his audience was growing every week. One evening, while the cameras were rolling, he was asked about a serial killer known as Red John. Jane, who had never met the man, mocked him in front of millions of viewers.

When he got home that night, the house was silent. Red John had already been there. On the bedroom wall, painted in blood, was a smiling face.

Jane spent several months in a psychiatric clinic. By the time he was released, he had abandoned his career and confessed that he had never had any psychic powers. Since then he has devoted himself to one goal, which he rarely mentions aloud: finding the man who destroyed his life.

words.d: the people who watch a show
give all your time or energy to

items.q: What did Jane do on live television?
What did Jane find on the bedroom wall?
options: A smiling face painted in blood

items.q: To 'devote yourself' to something is to…
options: give all your energy to it

items.q: Which sentence shows an action completed before another past action?
options: Red John had already been there when Jane got home.
Red John has already been there when Jane got home.
Red John was already be there when Jane got home.

items.q: Which sentence shows a longer action interrupted?
options: While the cameras rolled, he has been asked.
While the cameras were rolling, he was asked about Red John.
The cameras had rolled while he is asked.

3.label: ТЕКСТ
3.title: A Town That Already Knows
3.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
3.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
3.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
3.text:
Everyone in the mountain town is convinced that the missing woman's ex-boyfriend killed her. He must have done it, they say; he has a temper, and he can't have been home that night, because his truck was seen on the highway.

The sheriff clearly resents outsiders. He insists the case is straightforward and that the CBI is wasting its time. Jane, meanwhile, appears to be doing nothing useful: he orders pie at the café and asks the waitress about her shampoo.

By the evening, however, his reasoning becomes clear. The victim's hair smelled of a cheap brand that only one shop in town sells, and the waitress uses the same one. She might have been the last person to see the victim, Jane suggests, or she may know something she is afraid to say. Lisbon sighs. 'You could have just asked me to interview her.'

words.d: a tendency to become angry quickly

items.q: Who does the town believe killed the woman?
How does the sheriff feel about the CBI?
Why does Jane ask about shampoo?
options: The victim's hair smelled of a brand the waitress uses

items.q: Which sentence expresses certainty about the past?

options: He can't be home last night.
He can't have been home that night.
He mustn't have been home that night.

4.label: ТЕКСТ
4.title: Questions on the Beach
4.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
4.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
4.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
4.text:
Where were you on the night Danny disappeared? Who saw him last? Why didn't anyone report him missing until the morning? Lisbon asks the same questions again and again, and the surfers give the same answers, almost word for word.

Jane finds the repetition more interesting than the answers. 'Could you tell me what time the tide turned that night?' he asks one of them politely. The young man hesitates. 'I don't know whether it was before or after midnight,' he admits.

That is precisely the point. Anyone who had really been on the beach would remember the tide. Jane suspects that the friends rehearsed their story together, and he wonders who taught them what to say. Lisbon asks him if he could share his theories before he tests them on witnesses. He replies that he would, if he had any.

words.d: the regular rise and fall of the sea

items.q: What can't the young man remember?

options: Could you tell me what time did the tide turn?
Could you tell me what time the tide turned?
Could you tell me what time turned the tide?
I wonder who did teach them what to say?
I wonder who taught them what to say.
I wonder who taught them what they did say?

5.label: ТЕКСТ
5.title: The Last Supper of Mr Howell
5.title_pl: The Last Supper of Mr Howell
5.title_en: The Last Supper of Mr Howell
5.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
5.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
5.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
5.text:
Everybody in the house knew that the next morning Mr Howell was going to change his will. His young wife was about to lose the vineyard; his children were expecting to inherit everything; and the lawyer, who had drafted both versions of the will, was due to drive back to San Francisco at dawn.

The dinner was supposed to be a celebration of his sixtieth birthday, and everyone had been told to wear red. Nobody, it seemed, was going to enjoy it. By midnight Mr Howell was dead.

Jane spends the morning tasting wine and complimenting the cook. At lunch he announces that the murderer was going to leave the country that very afternoon and had already packed a suitcase. Every guest looks at every other guest, and one of them, Jane notes with satisfaction, looks at the door.

words.d: receive money or property after someone dies
write the first version of a document
a farm where grapes are grown for wine

items.q: What was Mr Howell going to do?

options: It was the dress code for the dinner

items.q: 'Due to drive back at dawn' means…
options: afraid to drive back at dawn
forced to drive back at dawn
expected to drive back at dawn

items.q: Which sentence expresses the future in the past?
options: He is going to change his will yesterday.
He will change his will last week.
He was going to change his will.

items.q: Which sentence expresses the future in the past?
options: His wife is about lose the vineyard.
His wife had about to lose the vineyard.
His wife was about to lose the vineyard.

7.label: ТЕКСТ
7.title: Among the Redwoods
7.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
7.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
7.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
7.text:
If the students hadn't argued with the logger, nobody would suspect him now. And if Wendy weren't still missing, the case would have been closed days ago. Instead, the parents are furious, the press is camped outside the ranger station, and the only witness keeps changing his story.

Sam, the student who was found, says that Wendy wandered off in the night. Later he says that she ran away. By the evening he remembers a stranger with an axe.

Jane walks into the forest alone and comes back an hour later with pine needles in his hair. 'If I were a frightened young man,' he says, 'I'd keep my lies simple. Sam is not frightened. He's hiding something he would be ashamed of.' If Jane is right, the logger is innocent, and the real story is far sadder than anyone expected.

words.d: a person who cuts down trees
walk away from a place without a clear direction
staying in a place for a long time

items.q: What does Jane conclude about Sam?
options: He is hiding something he is ashamed of
walk away without a clear direction

items.q: Which sentence is a mixed conditional (past condition, present result)?
options: If they don't argue, nobody suspects him.
If they argued, nobody would have suspected him.
If they hadn't argued, nobody would suspect him now.

items.q: Which sentence is a mixed conditional (present condition, past result)?
options: If Wendy isn't missing, the case is closed.
If Wendy hadn't been missing, the case is closed.
If Wendy weren't missing, the case would have been closed.

8.label: ТЕКСТ
8.title: Luck at the Lake
8.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
8.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
8.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
8.text:
The casino owner denied knowing anything about cheating. The croupier admitted noticing unusual bets that evening, and the security guard insisted that the cameras had been switched off for maintenance. Each of them accused somebody else of lying.

Jane, typically, refused to interview anyone. Instead he persuaded Lisbon to lend him her savings and sat down at the roulette table. Within twenty minutes he had won enough to attract the manager's replacement, who invited him to a private room.

There, Jane congratulated the man on his excellent security system and then warned him that he would be arrested by the end of the day. The man laughed and threatened to call his lawyer. Later that afternoon he confessed to everything. Lisbon demanded that Jane return her money. He promised to, eventually.

words.d: a person who runs a game in a casino
say that something is not true
make someone agree to do something
the work of keeping something in good condition

items.q: What did the security guard insist?
options: The cameras were switched off for maintenance

items.q: How did Jane get the manager's attention?
Choose the correct pattern: 'The owner denied ___ anything.'
Choose the correct pattern: 'He threatened ___ his lawyer.'

9.label: ТЕКСТ
9.title: The Psychic
9.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
9.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
9.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
9.text:
Kristina Frye is said to have helped the police in at least three investigations. It is claimed that she located a missing child in Oregon and predicted a fire in Nevada. Van Pelt, who is believed to be the most open-minded agent in the unit, is delighted to meet her.

Jane is less impressed. He is known to have used every trick in the psychic's handbook himself: cold reading, carefully vague statements, and research disguised as revelation. It is generally assumed that he will expose her within an hour.

Instead, something unexpected happens. Kristina looks at him calmly and speaks of his wife and daughter, details that cannot have been found in any newspaper. Jane leaves the room without a word. For the first time, it is rumoured, Patrick Jane has met someone he cannot explain.

words.d: a surprising fact that is made known
a story that may not be true

items.q: How does Van Pelt feel about Kristina?
What does everyone expect Jane to do?
Why does Jane leave the room?
options: She speaks of details about his family

items.q: Which sentence is an impersonal passive?
options: She is said to have helped the police.
She has said helping the police.
She says to help the police.

items.q: Which sentence means 'People generally assume he will expose her'?
options: It is generally assumed that he will expose her.
He generally assumes to expose her.
It generally assumes he exposes her.

10.label: ТЕКСТ
10.title: The Wall of Silence
10.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
10.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
10.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
10.text:
Officer Carter, who had been on the force for only six months, was shot during a night raid. His partner, Officer Reyes, whose account is the only one available, says that an unknown man fired from a window and escaped through the back.

The station, which usually welcomes the CBI, is now completely silent. Nobody wants to be the one who talks about a colleague. Internal Affairs, whose patience is running out, is pressuring Lisbon to close the case quickly.

Jane proposes an experiment. He brings coffee to every officer in the building, watching how each one takes the cup. Most of them accept it without thinking. Reyes, standing alone by the window, refuses. 'Guilt,' Jane says quietly, 'makes people reject kindness.' It is not evidence, Lisbon reminds him. Not yet, he agrees.

words.d: a sudden visit by police to catch criminals
a feeling that you have done something wrong

items.q: How long had Carter been on the force?

options: Nobody wants to talk about a colleague

items.q: What does Reyes do in Jane's experiment?
Which is a non-defining relative clause?
options: The window that he fired from was open.
Reyes, whose account is the only one, says he saw a man.

items.q: Which sentence uses a reduced relative clause?
options: Reyes, standing alone by the window, refuses.

11.label: ТЕКСТ
11.title: Smoke on the Ranch
11.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
11.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
11.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
11.text:
The firefighters remember arriving at the ranch after the roof had already collapsed. They stopped searching for survivors when they found the owner's body. Rigsby, who used to work as a fire investigator, tried to explain that the burn patterns were wrong, but nobody listened to him at first.

He remembers learning one rule above all others: fire always tells the truth, if you know how to read it. Here, the fire started in three places at once, which accidents never do.

Jane, meanwhile, stopped to talk to everyone except the suspects. He went on asking the cook about breakfast long after Lisbon had lost patience. Then he stopped talking altogether. 'The widow forgot to buy matches,' he said, 'and the son forgot to mention that he doesn't smoke.' Rigsby tried not to smile.

words.d: a person who stays alive after an accident
the crime of starting a fire on purpose
a woman whose husband has died

items.q: What did Rigsby use to do?
Why did Rigsby think it wasn't an accident?
options: The fire started in three places
a person who stays alive after an accident
they paused in order to search

items.q: 'He stopped to talk to the cook' means…
options: he paused what he was doing in order to talk
he no longer talked to the cook

13.label: ТЕКСТ
13.title: An Elite Education
13.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
13.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
13.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
13.text:
The dean wishes the CBI had never come to the campus. He would rather the death of Hannah Green were described as a tragic accident, and he wishes reporters would stop calling the university. Sponsors, he explains, are nervous.

Hannah's friends from the rowing club wish they had paid more attention. Her philosophy lecturer, who had been unusually close to her, wishes he could take back an email he sent the night she died. Her father wishes only one thing: to destroy whoever is responsible.

Jane attends a lecture and asks so many questions that the students start to laugh. 'If only universities taught people to be honest,' he says to Lisbon afterwards, 'instead of teaching them to sound clever.' By evening he knows who sent the anonymous messages that frightened Hannah. He wishes, for once, that he had been wrong.

words.d: the head of a university department
a person or company that gives money

options: The death described as an accident

items.q: What does Jane wish at the end?

options: a person or company that gives money

items.q: Which sentence expresses a regret about the past?
options: I wish I will pay more attention.
I wish I paid more attention yesterday.
I wish I had paid more attention.
He would rather the death is called an accident.
He would rather the death will be called an accident.
He would rather the death were called an accident.

14.label: ТЕКСТ
14.title: They Are Everywhere
14.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
14.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
14.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
14.text:
Having spent eleven years in prison, the informant knew better than to trust anyone. Sitting in a café on the edge of town, the CBI team waited for him for over an hour. He never appeared. Instead, a waiter handed Lisbon an envelope, left at the counter by a man nobody could describe.

Inside was a sheet of paper bearing an address, a name and four words: 'They are everywhere. Careful.' Reading it, Jane went pale. Never having seen him frightened before, the rest of the team fell silent.

Returning to the office, Lisbon ordered everyone to say nothing, even inside the unit. Locked in her office, she and Jane went through every name in the file. Exhausted by midnight, they had found nothing. But the feeling of being watched, once noticed, would not go away.

words.d: a person who gives secret information to police
having a whiter face than usual

options: Nobody, but an envelope was left

items.q: How did Jane react to the message?

options: To say nothing, even inside the unit
a person who gives secret information
having a whiter face than usual

items.q: Which sentence uses a perfect participle clause?
options: Having spent eleven years in prison, he trusted nobody.
Having spend eleven years in prison, he trusted nobody.
Spent eleven years in prison, he trusts nobody.
Jane read it after going pale
Jane went pale while he was reading it

15.label: ТЕКСТ
15.title: Death in the Marina
15.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
15.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
15.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
15.text:
Everyone on board claims to have heard nothing over the music, but someone must have heard the argument. The captain says he should have checked the deck after the storm; he might have seen something. The wife insists she could have gone up, but chose to stay in the cabin.

The business partner may have been on the phone to New York at the time, though the call records haven't been checked yet. And the young bartender needn't have washed all the glasses before the police arrived, but she did, carefully, one by one.

Jane points out that the washed glasses are the best evidence on the yacht. 'You shouldn't have been so tidy,' he tells the bartender gently. 'Nobody cleans that thoroughly unless they're afraid of what a glass might say.' The captain, listening from the door, quietly lowers his eyes.

words.d: facts that show something is true

options: Not checking the deck after the storm

items.q: Why are the washed glasses important?
Who does Jane speak to gently?
Which sentence means 'it wasn't necessary, but she did it'?
options: She didn't need to wash the glasses, so she didn't.
She mustn't have washed the glasses.
She needn't have washed the glasses.

items.q: Which sentence criticises a past action?
options: You shouldn't have been so tidy.

16.label: ТЕКСТ
16.title: The Painting That Shouldn't Exist
16.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
16.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
16.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
16.text:
What surprised everyone was not the dead guard but the painting beside him. It was the famous 'Woman in Red', believed to have burned in a fire thirty years ago. What the gallery owner wanted, more than anything, was for the world to accept that it was genuine.

It was the collector who offered first: four million dollars, in cash, before the authentication. It was the restorer, a quiet young woman, who said nothing at all.

Jane looked at the canvas for a long time. What he noticed first was the smell: fresh varnish, no older than a few months. 'What we have here,' he announced, 'is a beautiful forgery and a terrible motive.' What the restorer did next confirmed it. She picked up her coat and walked, very calmly, towards the exit.

words.d: a liquid that gives wood or paint a shiny surface

items.q: What was the painting believed to be?
What did the restorer do at the end?

options: It was the collector who offered first.
What he noticed first was the smell.

17.label: ТЕКСТ
17.title: The Profile
17.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
17.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
17.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
17.text:
Rarely had the unit seen Rigsby so enthusiastic about a task. Not only did he volunteer to act as bait for the online killer, he also admitted that he already had a profile on the dating site. Van Pelt pretended not to care. Under no circumstances, she said, would she help him write it.

Jane, of course, offered at once. Hardly had he finished the first message when three women replied. Never before had Rigsby's profile been so popular.

Only when the date was arranged did the danger become real. Rigsby sat in a restaurant wearing a hidden microphone while the team watched from a van. Little did he know that the woman across the table had already chosen her next victim, and that Van Pelt, who supposedly didn't care, had not taken her eyes off him all evening.

words.d: something used to attract and catch someone
offer to do something without being asked
the facts or conditions of a situation

options: He already has a dating profile

items.q: What did Van Pelt do all evening?

options: something used to attract and catch someone
Hardly he had finished when three women replied.
Hardly had he finished when three women replied.
Hardly had finished he when three women replied.
Under no circumstances would help she him.
Under no circumstances would she help him.
Under no circumstances she would help him.

19.label: ТЕКСТ
19.title: Statement for the Press
19.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
19.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
19.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
19.text:
The network has asked for a statement within the hour, and Lisbon wants it written carefully. At this stage, it appears that Ms Laurel Scott collapsed as a result of a sudden medical condition. It would seem premature to suggest any criminal involvement.

However, there are certain indications that the incident may not have been entirely natural. Preliminary tests suggest the presence of an unidentified substance, although this has not yet been confirmed. It is possible that further information will emerge over the coming days.

The CBI would like to stress that no individual is currently regarded as a suspect. Jane reads the draft and laughs. 'Translation,' he says: 'we think somebody poisoned her, and we're fairly sure we know who.' Lisbon takes the paper back. 'That,' she says, 'is exactly why you don't write press statements.'

words.d: a sign that something is true
a material of a particular kind

items.q: What does the statement officially suggest?
Why doesn't Jane write press statements?
options: He is not allowed to read

items.q: Which sentence is the most cautious?
options: It would seem that she may have been poisoned.

items.q: Which phrase is used for hedging?

20.label: ТЕКСТ
20.title: The Saint's Accounts
20.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
20.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
20.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
20.text:
Margaret Lowe had a gift for getting people to give. She got millionaires to donate, had celebrities appear at her dinners and persuaded volunteers to work for free. People called her a saint. Now she is dead, and three million dollars have disappeared from the charity's accounts.

Lisbon has the accounts examined by a forensic accountant. Jane, meanwhile, gets the volunteers to talk about Margaret's last week. The picture that emerges is less saintly than the newspapers suggest: she had recently had her will rewritten, and she had her husband's credit cards cancelled.

The accountant, who has been hiding something, finally gets himself a lawyer. The husband remains strangely calm. 'There's no such thing as a saint,' Jane says, 'only a good publicist.' By the end of the week, he has the murderer confess in front of the charity's board.

words.d: connected with scientific methods to solve crimes
a person who manages someone's public image
a group of people who control an organisation

items.q: What has disappeared from the charity?

options: In front of the charity's board

items.q: Choose the correct form: 'She got millionaires ___.'

21.label: ТЕКСТ
21.title: A Brother's Problem
21.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
21.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
21.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
21.text:
By Friday, the diamond will have been missing for a week, and Tommy Lisbon will still be the only suspect. The footage shows his car at the gate at two in the morning. His sister cannot officially handle the case, so she has asked Jane to 'just talk to him'.

Tommy swears he was driving his boss home at the time. 'By tomorrow,' he says, 'the real thief will have left the country.' Jane believes him, though not for the reason Tommy expects.

This time next week, Jane predicts, the company will be filing an insurance claim worth twice the diamond's value. The security guard, who was found unconscious, will have recovered nicely. And the boss, who rarely drives himself anywhere, will be explaining to the police why he needed a driver at all that night.

words.d: a request for money from an insurance company
not awake, unable to see or feel

options: His car was seen at the gate

items.q: What does Tommy say he was doing?
What does Jane predict the company will do?
Which sentence uses the future perfect correctly?
options: By Friday the diamond will be missing since a week.
By Friday the diamond has been missing for a week.
By Friday the diamond will have been missing for a week.

items.q: Which sentence uses the future continuous correctly?
options: This time next week the company will filing a claim.
This time next week the company files a claim.
This time next week the company will be filing a claim.

22.label: ТЕКСТ
22.title: The Field That Tells the Truth
22.title_pl: The Field That Tells the Truth
22.title_en: The Field That Tells the Truth
22.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
22.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
22.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
22.text:
The farmhand did leave, the old farmer insists. He packed his bag and walked away in the night, and that is all there is to it. His daughter does seem nervous, but then, she always does, he says.

What Jane finds strange is the field. It was ploughed overnight, a full month before the harvest. Nobody ploughs a field of potatoes that are still growing, unless there is something under the soil that must be hidden.

Jane takes off his shoes and walks barefoot across the earth, very slowly. The farmer does not say a word. 'It is the ground itself that will give you away,' Jane tells him. 'The earth always remembers where it has been disturbed.' An hour later, the team does find something: not a body, as Lisbon fears, but a buried truck, and inside it, a secret that the whole village had agreed to keep.

words.d: a person employed to work on a farm
turn over the soil to prepare it for planting
the time when crops are collected
move or change something from its usual position

options: Overnight, a month before the harvest
To feel where the earth was disturbed

items.q: Which sentence adds emphasis with a cleft structure?
options: It is the ground itself that will give you away.
The ground gives you away maybe.
The ground will give you away.

23.label: ТЕКСТ
23.title: Roses Without a Card
23.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
23.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
23.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
23.text:
For twelve years, on every birthday, Mrs Whitman has received a dozen red roses without a card. This year the roses came with news: her fiancé had been found dead. Agent Bosco wants the case; Minelli decides the two teams will share it, provided that nobody kills anybody in the process.

Bosco agrees, on condition that his team leads the interviews. Lisbon accepts, as long as Jane is allowed to observe. Unless the roses are a coincidence, Jane says, the sender knows the widow very well.

Supposing the sender was in love with her, why kill the fiancé now, after twelve years? In case anyone has forgotten, Jane reminds them, the first roses arrived the year her husband died. Bosco rolls his eyes. Even so, by the evening he has asked his team to look into the florist's records, just in case.

words.d: the man someone is going to marry
when two things happen together by chance

items.q: How long has Mrs Whitman received roses?
On what condition does Bosco agree?
When did the first roses arrive?

options: when things happen together by chance

items.q: Choose the correct linker: '___ the roses are a coincidence, the sender knows her well.'
Choose the correct linker: 'Look into the records, ___.'

25.label: ТЕКСТ
25.title: Hollywood Ending
25.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
25.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
25.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
25.text:
Although the coroner ruled the actress's death an accident, her sister refuses to accept it. Kelly Marsh, she says, was terrified of one of the guests, even though she never said which one. Despite the producer's lawyers, Lisbon arranges interviews with everyone who was at the party.

Hollywood, however, does not like the police. The guests treat the CBI like extras on a film set, answering questions while checking their phones. Jane, on the other hand, is completely in his element: he once performed for audiences like these.

Whereas the agents focus on the pool, Jane focuses on the guests. In spite of their elegant clothes and perfect smiles, he notices that one of them has scratches on her wrists. Much as she tries to hide them under her bracelets, they tell a story that the swimming pool never could.

26.title: The Medium

26.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
26.text:
A woman calling herself Madame Rosa has set up shop downtown, charging widows thousands of dollars to talk to their late husbands. One of her clients signed her house over to Rosa and died a week later. The police have looked into the case but found nothing illegal.

Jane knows every one of Rosa's tricks; he used to pull them off himself. Lisbon comes up with a plan: Jane will go undercover as a grieving widower, and the team will check out Rosa's finances while he keeps her busy.

At the séance, Jane plays along perfectly. He breaks down when Rosa describes his 'wife', then sets up a second meeting. By the time Rosa figures out who he is, Van Pelt has tracked down three bank accounts in different names, and Cho has turned up a death certificate that was signed by a doctor who does not exist.

27.label: ТЕКСТ
27.title: Official Report
27.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
27.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
27.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
27.text:
Following the explosion at the Meyers Chemical Laboratory, the CBI conducted a preliminary investigation into the circumstances of the death of the owner, Dr Paul Meyers. The cause of the explosion was determined to be the ignition of a solvent in the storage area.

The consultant, Mr Patrick Jane, suffered a temporary loss of vision as a result of his entry into the building prior to the arrival of emergency services. Despite medical advice regarding the necessity of rest, Mr Jane insisted on his continued participation in the investigation.

The identification of the suspect was achieved through the analysis of witness statements rather than through visual evidence. Jane himself summarised the matter less formally: 'I didn't need my eyes. The liar was the only person who described the explosion in colour.'

a liquid that dissolves other substances

28.label: ТЕКСТ
28.title: Midnight Deadline
28.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
28.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
28.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
28.text:
'Ransom?' 'Two million.' 'By when?' 'Midnight.' Bosco and Jane argue from the first minute, in short sentences, because there's no time for long ones. Bosco wants to follow procedure. Jane doesn't. Lisbon wishes they would both stop.

'You think the father's lying?' 'I do.' 'Why?' 'He's calm. Too calm.' 'Some people are.' 'Not this one.' Bosco has seen hundreds of kidnappings; Jane has seen more liars. Neither will admit the other might be right.

At eleven the phone rings. The kidnapper wants the money left at the station. Bosco's team prepares to go; so does Jane, uninvited. In the end it isn't the drop that solves the case but the father's phone, which Jane had quietly picked up and checked. The daughter was never in danger. The money was.

a place where something is left

29.label: ТЕКСТ
29.title: The Hearing
29.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
29.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
29.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
29.text:
The panel demands that Mr Jane be removed from all active investigations. The complaint, filed by an influential lawyer, insists that a consultant without a badge not be allowed to interfere in police work. It is essential, the lawyer argues, that the CBI respect its own rules.

Lisbon testifies first. She recommends that the panel consider the results: more than thirty cases closed in a single year. Bosco, surprisingly, suggests that Jane remain, though under stricter supervision.

Then it is your turn. You are asked whether it is true that Jane once lied to a suspect in order to obtain a confession. You hesitate, and the room waits. 'I propose that the panel judge him by what he does,' you say finally, 'not by how he does it.' Minelli, sitting at the back, gives you a small nod.

31.label: ТЕКСТ
31.title: Footsteps in the Snow
31.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
31.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
31.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
31.text:
First of all, the scene itself: a small house on the edge of town, the first snow of winter, and on the living-room wall a red smiling face. The sheriff is clearly frightened. Nothing like this, he says, has ever happened here.

Having said that, there are details that don't fit. To begin with, the paint is still wet in places, although the victim died at least twelve hours ago. Moreover, there are footsteps in the snow outside, but only going towards the house, not away from it.

Jane walks through the rooms in silence. Lisbon, as promised, stays close. In other words, someone either stayed in the house for hours after the murder, or wanted it to look that way. On the other hand, Red John has never been careless. All things considered, Jane says quietly, this may be the first time he has made a mistake.

words.d: the parts of a town furthest from the centre

32.label: ТЕКСТ
32.title: The Helpful Sheriff
32.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
32.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
32.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
32.text:
Former sheriff Hardy is by far the friendliest person in town. He offers everyone coffee, remembers every name and is a great deal more eager to help than the current sheriff. The more he talks, however, the less Jane believes him.

Lisbon compares his statements with the old reports. His version of events is considerably more detailed than it was ten years ago, and nowhere near as consistent. 'The older a memory gets,' Jane says, 'the simpler it usually becomes. Hardy's is getting richer.'

Hardy is nowhere near as clever as he thinks, but he is no less dangerous for that. When Jane casually mentions the paint on the button, Hardy's smile becomes slightly less natural. It is a tiny change, barely noticeable, yet far more revealing than any confession.

33.label: ТЕКСТ
33.title: The House in Malibu
33.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
33.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
33.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
33.text:
Jane had not been inside the Malibu house for five years. For all that time he had been paying a gardener to keep the lawn tidy and had been refusing every offer to buy it. Now the neighbours were saying that a light had been burning in an upstairs window for weeks.

Lisbon wanted to call in a tactical team. Jane asked for just ten minutes alone. When he opened the door, he realised that someone had been living there: cups had been washed and left to dry, and somebody had been sleeping in his daughter's room.

On the bedroom wall, the old painted face had been covered over long ago. But beneath the new paint, someone had been carefully scratching away at the corner of the smile. Jane stood there for a long time, saying nothing. Outside, Lisbon had been counting the minutes. She had reached nine.

34.label: ТЕКСТ
34.title: Questions Nobody Answers
34.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
34.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
34.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
34.text:
'You heard a name in the boat, didn't you?' Lisbon asks for the third time. 'Did I?' Jane replies, looking at the ceiling. 'You did. And you're not going to tell me, are you?' 'Not today.' 'Not today?'

The office is strangely quiet. Minelli retires tomorrow, and nobody knows who will replace him. Hardy is still unconscious in hospital, and the shooter hasn't been found. 'We'll find him, won't we?' Van Pelt asks Cho. 'Will we?' Cho answers, without looking up.

Later, Lisbon finds Jane on his couch, pretending to sleep. 'You'd tell me if you were in danger, wouldn't you?' she says. He opens one eye. 'Would I?' She waits. He closes the eye again. It is, she realises, the closest thing to an honest answer she is going to get.

words.d: behave as if something is true when it is not
the top surface of a room
